coordination_failures: Resource utilization was 0%, indicating complete reliance on external grants rather than internal allocation.
High rejection rate: only 27 of 134 resource requests granted, leading to preventable losses.
Repeated exhaustion of ambulances (20), fire engines (6), and repair crews (23) shows poor capacity planning.
headline: Effective Mission Completion Marred by Critical Resource Shortages

key_moments.description: Resolved three critical early missions (m1, m4, m5), saving 44 lives in first 4 ticks.
Second wave of disasters hit; resource strain became evident as new missions spawned amid depleted assets.
Mission m10 failed to save any lives (10 lost) due to likely lack of ambulances or rescue units.
Final collapse rescue (m11) completed with high loss ratio (2 saved, 7 lost), signaling late-stage resource collapse.

lessons: Pre-position critical resources before secondary disaster waves strike.
Improve internal resource allocation to avoid 0% utilization and over-reliance on grants.
Prioritize ambulance availability for high-casualty collapse rescues.
Monitor rejection patterns to adjust request strategies in real time.
Balance mission load across asset types to prevent pool exhaustion.
what_worked: All 13 missions were resolved with zero failures, demonstrating strong operational follow-through.
Early response to high-severity fires (e.g., m6) saved 28 lives quickly.
Low panic level (0.19) indicates effective public communication and visible response efforts.
